long_biography.plain_text:
Rodney Burwell paid for his studies at the University of North Dakota by running a cleaning business, which he sold to a professor on graduation. He studied industrial engineering and business administration, then served in the Army Corps of Engineers. Between overseas postings, he taught at Purdue and coached its rifle team to a conference championship.

His connection with the Dakotas later shaped a business partnership. As a boy, Burwell had worked on the Cronin family farm near Gettysburg, South Dakota, and remained friends with Dan Cronin. The two bought the town’s John Deere dealership to keep it open. That local purchase became C & B Operations, a chain serving farming communities across several states.
